Re: Internal Appeal of Prior Authorization Denial  
Member: Riley Brooks  
Member ID: W997409334  
Plan: Molina Healthcare Commercial/ACA, Mississippi  
Requested service: Rotator cuff repair  
CPT: 29827  
Reference number: POC-AA9EA32E7D-95281  

Dear Molina Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827. Please treat this as my request for an internal review of the adverse benefit determination.

The stated basis for the denial was that the submitted records did not show an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. The clinical records demonstrate that conservative treatment was substantial, appropriately directed, and unsuccessful:

- I had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that continued despite rest.
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 1, 2026, through June 24, 2026, including 16 visits. The therapy specifically addressed rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics. This treatment is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 19, 2026. It provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I remain unable to lift the affected arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing and range-of-motion limitation caused by pain.
- MRI on June 16, 2026, demonstrated a 1.8 cm full-thickness supraspinatus tear with grade 2 fatty atrophy.

These records directly address the requirement for a meaningful trial of nonoperative treatment. They show failure of rest, medication, supervised physical therapy, and injection treatment, followed by persistent functional impairment and objective structural pathology. The MRI findings and continued loss of function support the medical necessity of surgical repair.

The records also document the absence of relevant contraindicating conditions: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker. The requested procedure was submitted by Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery.

I request that Molina overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29827. If Molina maintains the denial, please provide the complete clinical-review criteria used for this decision, including the specific MCG or other criteria applicable to CPT 29827, the version used, its effective date, and the precise criteria that Molina contends were not met. The publicly available Molina shoulder-arthroscopy material I was able to locate directs reviewers to MCG criteria for rotator cuff repair, but the specific criteria were not publicly available in the material I could retrieve. I have not quoted the plan’s policy here because I was unable to retrieve the complete criteria applied to this request.

Please include all of the submitted clinical records in the review, including the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection record, MRI report, examination findings, and orthopedic surgery documentation. Please send the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Riley Brooks
